title: Search a binary search tree
prompt: root is a binary search tree: smaller values are to the left of each node, and larger values to the right. Return true when target is in the tree. Follow one path from the root: the last check allows 60 looks at a value in a tree of 4,095 nodes.
hints: At each node, what does comparing the target with the node's value tell you about where to go?
Smaller means go left, larger means go right, equal means found.
Loop while the node is not null. Returning false after the loop covers a value that is not there.
checkLabels: 9 is not in the sample tree.
A value down the right side is found.
A value that needs a left turn after right turns is found.
It finds a value among 4,095 nodes.
It reports a missing value among 4,095 nodes.
Follow one path. Look at no more than 60 values in the tree of 4,095 nodes.

wrongAnswers.misconception: Goes right for a smaller target and left for a larger one.
Searches both subtrees of every node, which ignores the ordering.

feedback: A binary search tree lets you discard one whole subtree at every node. If your code can visit both sides of a node, it is doing too much.
